Thanks Megan — looping internal interviewers to align on scope and leveling for this hire. I read the packet and I think Alex fits the senior->staff band; the interview needs to probe system thinking at scale, kernel/compilation tradeoffs, and evidence of leading cross-functional rollouts.

High-level ask to interviewers:
- Explicitly capture evidence of "influence and ownership" (examples of driving infra design across teams).
- Leveling anchors: Staff = owns a cross-product latency/cost improvement end-to-end, sets tradeoffs for the org, mentors SDE2+ engineers.
- Focus areas per slot (suggested):
  1) System design (60m) — workload shapes, batching strategies, KV cache behavior, fallback policies.
  2) Performance & cost tradeoffs (45m) — quantization decisions, kernel selection rationale, throughput/latency measurement approaches.
  3) Behavioral & leadership (30m) — conflict with partners, roadmap tradeoffs, mentoring examples.

I attached an interviewer rubric and a short system-design prompt PDF. Please review and flag any redlines by EOD so I can push back to recruiting if we need to swap the candidate level or interviewers.

Attachments: staff_serving_interviewer_rubric.xlsx, system_design_prompt.pdf

Thanks — Rishi

Thanks Rishi — quick notes from my read:

- Agree on making system design the first loop — we want to see mental model earliest. If they stumble there, it’s harder to recover in later slices.
- Add a 15-minute "operational incident" mini-case inside the behavioral slot: recent outage post-migration where they had to trade latency vs safety. That will reveal bias for action and pragmatic tradeoffs.
- For the performance slot, please call out expectation to quantify impact (e.g., what metrics would you instrument, how would you measure KV cache hit/miss on a live fleet).

Minor logistics: I can cover the performance slot if needed; otherwise happy to be the bar-raiser for the behavioral portion.

Rishi / Marissa — thanks for the summary. Few bar-raiser notes:

- Leveling clarity: To call someone "Staff" we need two lines of evidence: (1) scope/breadth — led multiple cross-team projects affecting platform-level SLAs, (2) sustained influence — recommendations adopted by product/infra leaders. Concrete examples > theoretical answers. Ask for artifacts (slides, PR links) where they led the change.
- Probe for tradeoff frameworks: if they cannot state measurable success criteria or a roll-forward plan, treat that as a concern.
- Red flags: inability to decompose longitudinal ownership (e.g., only tactical fixes), poor collaborator feedback, or lack of mentoring examples.

One scheduling ask: I prefer the behavioral/bar-raiser slot after system design (so we have concrete engineering examples to challenge).

I'll volunteer to be the bar-raiser in the behavioral slot; happy to prep a short set of 3 follow-ups for any strong/suspect answers.

Lauren Bishop
